questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
In the diagram, a firm increases its output from OY to OZ. MC costs, revenue AR O Y Z output Which statement about the effect on economic efficiency is correct?

options.A: It will increase because a greater quantity will be produced and higher total revenue will be earned.
options.B: It will increase because the value that consumers place on the product comes closer to the cost of producing the last unit.
options.C: It will decline because both average and marginal revenue will fall.
options.D: It will decline because both total and marginal cost will rise.

questions.questionText: A proposal for a new power station was rejected by the government because it was not socially beneficial. The government calculated that the private costs would be $800m, private benefits $900m and external benefits $300m. What must have been true about the external costs of the power station?

options.A: External costs were equal to external benefits.
options.B: External costs were greater than $400m.
options.C: External costs were less than external benefits.
options.D: There were no external costs.

questions.questionText: What will happen if, in response to a fall in its price, a consumer buys more of a good?

options.A: a fall in the total utility derived from consuming the good
options.B: a movement along the consumer’s demand curve
options.C: a rise in the marginal utility derived from consuming the good
options.D: a shift in the consumer’s demand curve

What is one of the long-term benefits to a firm of vertical integration?

options.A: a concentration on activities in which the firm has a comparative advantage
options.B: a reduction in the total costs involved in agreeing contracts with other firms
options.C: an increase in the firm’s market share
options.D: improvements in efficiency resulting from increased use of market incentives

questions.questionText: The organisers of a major sporting event produce official souvenir products. Cheaper unofficial souvenirs are also produced by street traders who sell them to people walking to the event. Of what is this an example?

options.A: a contestable market
options.B: perfect competition
options.C: price discrimination
options.D: price leadership

questions.questionText: Which assumption is made in calculating a firm’s short-run production function?

options.A: All factors of production are fixed.
options.B: All factors of production are variable.
options.C: The state of technology is fixed.
options.D: The state of technology is variable.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, TC is a firm’s short-run total cost curve. TC costs O Q Q Q
The table shows the total cost of a firm. total cost output $ 0 40
Which condition must apply before a market can be regarded as perfectly contestable?

options.A: All firms in the industry are price-takers.
options.B: All firms in the industry produce an identical product.
options.C: There are a large number of firms in the industry.
options.D: There are zero costs of entry to, and exit from, the industry.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the average and marginal revenue curves of an oligopolistic firm. OQ is the profit-maximising output. Which curve could be the firm’s marginal cost curve? A MR B C D costs/ revenue AR MR O Q output
What is most likely to be found when comparing the long-run equilibrium outcome in monopolistic competition with that in perfect competition?

options.A: a greater degree of excess capacity in monopolistic competition
options.B: a higher level of profit in monopolistic competition
options.C: a larger number of firms in monopolistic competition
options.D: a more price-elastic demand curve in monopolistic competition

questions.questionText: Which is not a source of market failure?

options.A: imperfect information
options.B: income inequality
options.C: monopoly
options.D: non-excludability

questions.questionText: The government wants to regulate the consumption of a demerit good in order to increase society’s net welfare. In which situation will society’s net welfare increase?

options.A: The fall in the marginal social benefit is greater than the fall in the marginal social cost.
options.B: The fall in the marginal social cost is greater than the fall in the marginal social benefit.
options.C: The fall in the total social benefit is greater than the fall in the total social cost.
options.D: The fall in the total social cost is greater than the fall in the total social benefit.

questions.questionText: Which measure is least likely to help a household out of the poverty trap?

options.A: changing a universal benefit to a means-tested benefit
options.B: increasing the threshold at which income tax is paid
options.C: introducing a national minimum wage
options.D: reducing the basic rate of income tax

questions.questionText: ‘The addition to revenue which results from employing one additional unit of a factor of production, the quantities of all other factors of production remaining constant’. What does this define?

options.A: marginal factor cost
options.B: marginal revenue
options.C: marginal revenue product
options.D: the law of diminishing returns

Over a given period the amount of overtime worked in manufacturing industry increases. What is likely to be a consequence of this?

options.A: a decrease in employment
options.B: a decrease in the rate of inflation
options.C: a more rapid growth in average earnings than in hourly wage rates
options.D: a more rapid growth in manufacturing output than in productivity

questions.questionText: What is a common characteristic of developing economies?

options.A: a relatively small agricultural sector
options.B: extensive underemployment
options.C: high saving rates
options.D: stable export earnings

questions.questionText: The diagram shows data on various aspects of four countries. Which country is likely to be least developed? % of population in rural areas key country A country B country C country D average years life expectancy of schooling at birth (years) GDP per capita (US$ PPP)
If the marginal propensity to consume in an economy in a given period becomes greater than unity, this must mean that

options.A: consumers will be spending more than they are earning.
options.B: inflation will be generated in the economy.
options.C: the country will suffer a trade deficit.
options.D: the marginal propensity to save will be negative.

options.A: (cid:1) (cid:1) (cid:2)

questions.questionText: What would cause an increase in the transactions demand for money?

options.A: a fall in the price of bonds
options.B: an increase in nominal national income
options.C: an increase in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase in unemployment

questions.questionText: Government economic advisers disagree over the relative impact of fiscal and monetary controls. What is most likely to be the first stage at which a time lag will occur?

options.A: in the introduction of the chosen policy
options.B: in the operational effectiveness of the policy
options.C: in the recognition of the existence of the problem
options.D: in the selection of the appropriate policy

questions.questionText: What has not accompanied global economic growth over the last twenty five years?

options.A: a depletion of non-renewable resources
options.B: decreased international trade
options.C: growing urbanisation
options.D: increased atmospheric pollution

questions.questionText: Which policy pursued by a central bank represents a contractionary monetary policy?

options.A: a reduction in the interest rate at which it will lend to banks
options.B: a reduction in the minimum cash to deposit ratios of banks
options.C: the purchase of foreign currency to influence the country’s exchange rate
options.D: the sale of government bonds in the open market

questions.questionText: Which policy’s principal aim is to ensure sound public finances?

options.A: environmental policy
options.B: fiscal policy
options.C: monetary policy
